task: Physics language model — autoregressive next-token generation of quantum-physics sentences on a CLLN NMOS input-output fully-connected network, trained end-to-end on real ngspice. Reduced 122-token vocabulary (plus a <BOS> start marker; 123 symbols); 4 grammatical shapes including questions.

network.structure: 122 output branches x 112 gate inputs, input-output fully-connected NMOS network. Input = 7-token context x 16-D SciBERT-FA embedding = 112 gate voltages; output = 122 physical branch drain voltages, read as next-token logits via a masked softmax (123 symbols = 122 vocabulary tokens + a masked <BOS>).
network.device: NMOS (VTO=0.75 V) + series resistance, gate floor 0.4 V; input-output fully-connected network (one shared drain node per branch)
network.embedding: SciBERT frozen-adapter 16-D (scibert_fa16.json), FactorAnalysis refit for the 122-token vocabulary (plus <BOS>)

corpus.shows_in: [det] [quantum-state] shows [outcome] in the [medium] .  (also short form: [det] [state] shows [outcome] .)
corpus.question: what is the [head] ?   (interrogative; exercises the ? / what / is tokens)
corpus.design: Four grammatical shapes (measure-of, has-in, shows-in, what-is question). The subject determiner spans all 7 openers (the/a/an/this/that/each/every); object determiners are fixed to 'the' (removes the autoregressive a/an-agreement trap). The corpus is 6998 unique valid sentences (5762 train + 1236 test), all grammatical.
examples: a qudit shows entanglement in the insulator .
every resonator measures voltage of the qubit .
that fermion has charge in the condensate .
this interferometer measures charge of the proton .

data_splits.note: The fixed test-window sample is reused at every epoch and never contributes to gate-voltage updates.

operating_point: readout temperature T=0.0006 (validity-max). Generation-vs-training temperatures differ (train T=0.0025).
generation_standard: STANDARD 1000-sentence test = autoregressive next-token generation with mixed openers (per-sentence uniform over the/a/an/this/that/each/every, a|an agreement-correct), readout T=0.0006.

headline.note: Device-faithful (real ngspice .op free solves, five 1000-sentence batches): 1.0000 clean validity, 4 distinct grammatical shapes including questions, 7 distinct sentence openers.

noise_table.description: Noise-resident 1x model: each chip = a fixed per-transistor Vth-mismatch fingerprint (sigma=10 mV = 1.3% of VTO) + per-device drive-strength (kp) mismatch (sigma=0.5%) + read noise (sigma=2.25 mV = 0.5% of the 0.45 V input rail), whole-training on real ngspice. Device-faithful mixed-opener validity (real ngspice, five 1000-sentence batches, T=0.0006).
noise_table.noise_cost: noise costs only ~0.2% (clean 1.0000 -> noise-mean 0.9979); 1x model = per-device Vth + drive-strength mismatch + read noise -> highly noise-robust.

training.rule: per-sample contrastive coupled learning, strict batch-1 SGD, one-hot CE target, K=1: free solve (real ngspice) -> clamp outputs to the CE target -> contrastive gate update per edge, clip [0.4, 8.0]
training.balanced_sampling: the question family is upweighted during sampling so it gets enough exposure (~700 samples) relative to the high-fanout declarative shapes.
training.simulator: FREE phase = real ngspice .op (in-circuit); CLAMP phase = clamped-output solve.

status: Reduced-vocab CLLN language model: clean 1.0000 + 3 noise chips (mean 0.9979), device-faithful on real ngspice; 13,664 edges, 122-token vocabulary (plus <BOS>), 4 grammatical shapes including questions.
